reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of sign-gestalt formation lies in how formal stimulus arrangements—particularly those enabling simultaneous visual access—facilitate rapid learning. This is modeled as a conditional process where the presence of a stimulus configuration S leads to a gestalt G, governed by a learning rate L. The coup d'oeil principle further refines this by optimizing the spatial-temporal alignment of stimuli to reduce cognitive processing delay. Formal conditionality law extends this by asserting that the efficacy of such learning is determined not by the material properties of the stimulus but by its presentation format. These primitives form a dual framework: one rooted in Bayesian inference over stimulus configurations (GSI), and another in state-transition dynamics of perceptual integration (GSE). Failure modes arise when formal conditions are inconsistent or when perceptual closure fails due to fragmented or ambiguous input.
